summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: almost every Hindi video gets 100 to 1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 30 views. The best videos explain a surprising 'how does it know?' trick about a familiar device (PIR motion sensor, clap switch, robot avoiding walls), and those also get the shares and saves. Near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector videos, two IR sensor videos, two tap videos) and the newest video, which has barely any data yet, are not adding anything.
winningPattern: A common object or 'magic' behavior explained by one hidden sensor, on Instagram Reels in Hindi. The title opens with a myth-busting or curiosity line ('Aapko Dekhta Nahi!', 'Taali Nahi, Sirf Shor Sunta Hai', 'Robot Deewar Se Kaise Bachta Hai?') followed by the sensor name, and the idea is simple enough to grasp in one sentence. Titles that flip an assumption (it doesn't see you, it doesn't hear claps) beat plain 'how does X detect Y' titles. Shares and saves come from robot and DIY-relevant topics that makers want to build.
doMore: Post Instagram-first and treat YouTube as secondary until its Hindi reach improves
Open titles with a surprising negative claim that flips what people assume ('X nahi, sirf Y')
Pick topics with a maker angle (clap switch, robot, PIR) since they earn saves and shares
Add a closing line that invites a share or save, such as 'Apne dost ko bhejo jo robot bana raha hai'
Check which hooks work after 48 hours, then make a follow-up to each top video
stopDoing: Making several near-identical videos on one sensor (smoke, tap, IR) within the same week
Plain 'Kaise kaam karta hai?' titles with no surprise or myth to bust
Mixing English into a Hindi channel, as the English Arduino video got no Instagram views
